title: West Brom deducted two points by EFL after financial regulation breach
content:
West Bromwich Albion have been docked two points for breaching the English Football League’s (EFL) profitability and sustainability rules (PSR).

The sanction sees them drop from 18th to 20th in the Championship, six points clear of relegation, with two games to play.

The fast-tracked decision, which was made by the EFL’s independent Club Financial Review Panel on Friday, confirms Leicester City’s relegation to League One and means Oxford United, currently third from bottom on 44 points, will need to win their remaining games against Sheffield Wednesday and Millwall to have any chance of catching either Charlton Athletic or West Brom, who are tied on 50 points.

West Brom, on the other hand, need only a point from their two remaining fixtures – Saturday’s home match against Ipswich Town and next Saturday’s visit to Sheffield Wednesday – to guarantee their survival. Their goal difference is also bigger than both Charlton’s and Oxford’s.

West Ham disputed the decision via a statement that read: “The club disagrees with the Club Financial Review Panel’s (CFRP) findings and remains of the view that it has fully complied with the Profitability and Sustainability (P&S) Rules.

“West Bromwich Albion has not been informed of the quantum of the breach, save that this is less than £2million. This is therefore the smallest ever breach of the P&S Rules across the EFL Championship and the Premier League.

“Proceedings were brought by the EFL’s Club Financial Reporting Unit (CFRU) following a change in the CFRU’s approach to Community Development Expenditure. In 2023/24, the CFRU accepted that the club was entitled to include in-kind donations of the Club’s facilities, staff time and resources to its official charity partner, The Albion Foundation, in its P&S calculation. Earlier this year, the CFRU informed the club that it had changed its approach and imposed a retrospective adjustment to the Club’s P&S calculation.

“Without the CFRU changing its approach to the Community Development Expenditure, the club would not have breached the P&S Rules.  West Bromwich Albion has a right of appeal and is considering its options.

“The club will provide further comment once it has received the written reasons. For now, we will settle this on the pitch.”

The PSR breach relates to the three-season stretch that ended last summer, a period that saw the West Midlands-based club lose £64million ($86million), £22.5million over the permitted loss threshold of £41.5million. Teams that overshoot this limit can face a deduction of 12 points.

However, the EFL allows teams to deduct any money they spend on their academies, community projects, infrastructure, and women’s teams. In West Brom’s case, this reduced their breach to less than £2million.

Under the league’s sanctioning guidelines, a breach of this size is reduced to just three points. A further point was shaved off West Brom’s sanction because their financial loss for 2024/25 was significantly less than the previous season’s.

The club had hoped they might get another point back for “exceptional cooperation,” but the panel decided not to award any further mitigation.

An appeal is possible, but it would appear unlikely, as West Brom would only do so if Oxford overtake them, and the EFL will be pleased this matter was dealt with so quickly. Both parties have 14 days from the ruling’s publication to lodge an appeal.

It has been a disappointing campaign for West Brom, who have yo-yoed between English football’s top two divisions in recent decades, but they are finishing the season in good form under interim manager James Morrison and will be confident of avoiding the drop.

They become, however, the third Championship team to be docked points this season, following the earlier punishments for Leicester and Sheffield Wednesday, who lost six and 18 points, respectively.
